claims.quote: 'Hot nose' on cerebral perfusion scan = brain death sign

claims.quote: c. claims.quote: b. Items 2–7 have been confirmed AND (done when components of the examination or apnea testing cannot be completed or when results of the examination are uncertain) An EEG shows electrocortical silence.

claims.text: Aspects (abnorm in red) Dx: serial determination of clin criteria showing permanent loss of brain funct, incl that of the brain stem; apnea testing; sometimes EEG, brain vasc imaging, or both
claims.quote: Serial determination of clinical criteria to demonstrate permanent loss of brain function, including that of the brain stem Apnea testing Sometimes electroencephalography (EEG), brain vascular imaging, or both

claims.text: EEG or brain perf tests are sometimes used to confirm absence of brain activity or blood flow but are ⍉USU required; they are indicated when apnea testing = ⍉hemodynamically tolerated and when only 1 neuro exam = desirable (eg, to expedite organ procurement for transplantation)
claims.quote: Sometimes EEG or tests of brain perfusion are used to confirm absence of brain activity or brain blood flow and thus provide additional evidence to family members, but these tests are not usually required. They are indicated when apnea testing is not hemodynamically tolerated and when only 1 neurologic examination is desirable (eg, to expedite organ procurement for transplantation).

claims.text: Required b4 declaring: a known catastrophic and permanent brain inj; a struct or met cause of brain damage; use of potentially anesthetizing or paralyzing meds and illicit drugs excluded; potentially reversible met abnormalities (incl hypoglycemia and acid-base and lyte abnormalities) excluded
claims.quote: For a clinician to declare brain death (see table ) (1), the following requirements must be met: A known catastrophic and permanent brain injury must have occurred. A structural or metabolic cause of brain damage must be present. Use of potentially anesthetizing (including nervous system depressants and alcohol) or paralyzing medications and illicit drugs, especially self-administered, must be excluded. Potentially reversible metabolic abnormalities, including hypoglycemia and acid-base and electrolyte abnormalities, must be excluded.

claims.text: Assessment should ⍉begin until ± 24 hrs after a brain inj capable of causing brain death; if hypothermia = present, a core temp < 36° C must be ↑slowly to > 36° C for ≥ 24 hrs; SBP should be ≥ 100 mm Hg and MAP maintained @ ≥ 75 mm Hg
claims.quote: Brain death assessment should not begin until at least 24 hours after a brain injury capable of causing brain death. If hypothermia is present, a core temperature < 36° C must be increased slowly to > 36° C for ≥ 24 hours. Systolic blood pressure should be ≥ 100 mm Hg, and mean arterial pressure should be maintained at ≥ 75 mm Hg.

claims.text: Exam includes pupil reactivity, oculovestibular, oculocephalic and corneal reflexes, and apnea testing
claims.quote: Examination includes Assessment of pupil reactivity Assessment of oculovestibular, oculocephalic, and corneal reflexes Apnea testing

claims.text: Apnea test: despite the passively rising PaCO2, brain death requires the absence of spont respirations, a pH of < 7.30, and a PaCO2 of ≥ 60 mm Hg and ≥ 20 mm Hg above the pt's baseline
claims.quote: Despite the ventilatory stimulus of the passively rising PaCO2, brain death requires the absence of spontaneous respirations, a pH of < 7.30, and a PaCO2 of ≥ 60 mm Hg and ≥ 20 mm Hg above the patient's baseline.

claims.text: Adults: ± 1 complete assessment must be done, and ± 1 additional exam by the same or another indep clinician = recommended to reduce the risk of a false-positive assessment; for children, some states advise 2 separate examinations by indep clinicians separated by ± 48 hrs
claims.quote: At least 1 complete brain death assessment by a clinician must be done for an adult, but doing at least 1 additional brain death examination subsequently by the same or another independent clinician is recommended to reduce the risk of a false-positive assessment. For children, some states advise clinicians to do 2 separate examinations by independent clinicians separated by at least 48 hours (1).

claims.text: Eti Ventilators and meds can perpetuate cardiopulm and other body functions despite complete cessation of all cerebral activity; total cessation of integrated brain funct, esp that of the brain stem, = accepted legally and culturally in most of the world as a person's death
claims.quote: The concept of brain death developed because ventilators and medications can perpetuate cardiopulmonary and other body functions despite complete cessation of all cerebral activity. The determination that brain death/death by neurologic criteria (ie, total cessation of integrated brain function, especially that of the brain stem) constitutes a person’s death has been accepted legally and culturally in most of the world.

claims.text: Sx Brain death = ⍉declared or assessed if the pt = breathing spontaneously, can be aroused, = ⍉in coma, or has intact brain stem reflexes
claims.quote: Brain death should not be declared or considered and brain death assessment should not be done if any of the following is present: The patient is breathing spontaneously. The patient can be aroused. The patient is not in coma. The patient has intact brain stem reflexes.

claims.text: During terminal apnea, spinal motor reflexes may occur (arching of the back, neck turning, stiffening of the legs, UE flex: the so-called Lazarus sign); family members who wish to be present when the ventilator = shut off need to be warned
claims.quote: Spinal motor reflexes may occur during terminal apnea; they include arching of the back, neck turning, stiffening of the legs, and upper extremity flexion (the so-called Lazarus sign). Family members who wish to be present when the ventilator is shut off need to be warned of such reflex movements.

claims.text: Tx and next step The dx of brain death = equivalent to the person's death; after confirmation, all supporting ♡ and resp treatments are ended, and cessation of ventilatory support results in terminal arrhythmias
claims.quote: The diagnosis of brain death is equivalent to the person’s death. After brain death is confirmed, all supporting cardiac and respiratory treatments are ended. Cessation of ventilatory support results in terminal arrhythmias.

claims.text: B4 the exam, the family or caregivers should be informed of the process and offered the opportunity to witness the eval, which may help them accept that brain death has occurred
claims.quote: Before the examination for brain death, the patient's family or caregivers should be informed of the process and be offered the opportunity to witness the brain death evaluation process, which may help them accept that brain death has occurred.
